_status: Module 4, Lesson 4.1 'When a device is lost' (learner guide of 21 October 2026): the 3S test from Module 1 (NPC Circular 16-03, Section 11) applied to a lost device; encryption turns 'we lost the data' into 'we lost a device'. Fictional cases.

scenarios.text: Sol's field laptop is stolen from a car. It holds 300 applicants' case notes and scanned IDs, and the disk is not encrypted.
scenarios.why: Sensitive data, reason to believe someone unauthorized has it, and a real risk of serious harm: it can be notifiable, and the 72-hour clock may already be running. Report at once, so IT can try to lock or wipe it.

scenarios.text: The same laptop is stolen, but full-disk encryption is on, and its password was never written down or kept with it.
scenarios.why: The thief has scrambled bytes: encryption turned "we lost the data" into "we lost a device". Still report it at once and record it as an incident; the DPO decides.
